speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are a pregnant patient experiencing fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. To better assist you, have you noticed any specific rash or sensitivity to light?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. The consumption of ice cream three days prior is a bit unusual; could you clarify if this was the only food you ate that day, or if you recall eating anything else, particularly unpasteurized dairy or soft cheeses? Have you experienced any muscle aches or joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever. I also have Headache, Anorexia, Fatigue, Malaise.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeriosis (Listeria monocytogenes infection).

The history of eating ice cream three days before symptom onset, combined with fever, headache, and anorexia in a pregnant patient, is highly suggestive of Listeriosis, which can be caused by unpasteurized dairy products.
